Hi Sean,

Thanks for the SIG responses you sent last week. Our security team reviewed the data handling sections and asked for a few clarifications so we can close out the questionnaire:

1) Data retention: we need the default retention period for prompt logs, embeddings, and full request/response records for hosted customers, and whether customers can configure that retention per account.

If possible, could you provide a short attestation letter we can add to our vendor file and any supporting docs (data retention policy, architecture diagram) as attachments?

We'd like to have this wrapped up by Jan 20. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Hi Rajesh —

Appreciate the callout. Below are point-by-point clarifications you can paste into the SIG spreadsheet and the attestation language we'd include in a short letter. I'll attach the policy and an architecture diagram as requested.

1) Data retention (hosted/default):
- Prompt logs (full request/response pairs): default retention is 30 days for hosted API customers.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: default retention is 90 days.
- Aggregated usage telemetry (metrics): retained for 365 days.
- Customers on Redwood Dedicated or Private can configure retention via account settings or via contract addendum; hosted customers can request retention changes through support.

2) Prompt/log storage and access:
- Storage: prompt logs are stored in encrypted object storage in the primary region where the tenant is hosted (US customers: us-west-2 by default).
- Encryption: data at rest is encrypted with AES-256; keys are managed in our KMS (customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private deployments).
- Access: access to raw prompt logs is restricted to a small, audited set of support and SRE roles; access requires Just-in-Time approval and is logged. Customer success or account teams do NOT have default access to raw prompt content.

3) Training on customer data:
- Redwood does not use customer prompt or message content to further train, fine-tune, or update our hosted model weights by default.
- We may use aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry (e.g., token usage patterns, model latency metrics) to improve system performance; we do not retain or use identifiable prompt text for model training unless an explicit opt-in is agreed in contract and the customer provides consent.

Attestation language (suggested):
"Redwood Inference confirms that, for hosted customers by default, prompt and full request/response logs are retained for 30 days and are not used to train or fine-tune hosted production models unless an explicit opt-in agreement is in place. Access to prompt logs is limited to authorized operations personnel with audit logging and just-in-time approvals in place."

Attachments included:
- redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf (PDF, 82 KB)
- prompt-log-architecture-diagram.png (PNG, 210 KB)
- customer-data-training-attestation.docx (DOCX, 12 KB)

If you'd like, we can produce a signed attestation on Redwood letterhead for Finly procurement. Would that work?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Rajesh —

Quick answers:
- We do not apply automatic PII redaction to prompt logs at collection time. We recommend customers use client-side redaction or instruct app teams to remove sensitive fields before sending. For support investigations we apply redaction tooling as part of the access workflow and require justification and JIT approval.
- Opt-in training: that is handled via an addendum to the services agreement that specifies scope of data used, minimum anonymization requirements, retention, and compensation. I've copied the legal-friendly clause below for your procurement team to review; Monica's team can provide a redlineable sample addendum if you want to move forward.

Sample clause (for review):
"Customer Data Training Addendum: Customer may elect to opt-in to allow Redwood to use Customer Data (as defined in the Agreement) to train or fine-tune Redwood models only upon execution of a mutually agreed addendum. The addendum will specify the exact data scope, permitted transformations (e.g., irreversible hashing, token-level redaction), retention period, and any commercial terms. Redwood will not use Customer Data for model training without such a signed addendum."

Next steps: Monica will drop a signed attestation PDF to the Drive link I shared and copy you when uploaded. Marissa will follow up to schedule a quick 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through the controls.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: customer-data-training-attestation.pdf (attached to Drive link)
